paper.title: MDTeamGPT: A Self-Evolving LLM-based Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Disciplinary Team Medical Consultation
paper.central_claim: Residual specialist discussion and outcome-grounded dual knowledge bases enable self-evolving medical consultation, improving diagnostic rationality, accuracy and transferable reasoning.

provenance.notes: Runtime context identifies gpt-6.1-sol; no independently exported actual-model receipt/session identifier available; no model probing performed.

sections_read: Entire supplied text §§1–5, Algorithms 1–2, Tables 1–4, all Appendices A/B, prompt templates, detailed cases, ethics and human evaluation.
materials.notes: All 3009 lines read. No page images supplied; numeric claims restricted to text/tables, not inferred figure bars. No code run or medical system deployed.

evidence.quote: We randomly selected five questions from the MedQA dataset and five questions from the PubMedQA dataset, resulting in a total of 10 test questions.

evidence.quote: the volunteers assigned relatively low scores to the "Efficiency" metric, primarily due to the increased time required for multi-round discussions among multiple roles compared to the Single-Agent approach.

evidence.quote: If votes are evenly distributed, the final answer is randomly selected from the agents’ choices.
evidence.support_explanation: Discussion bound and tie fallback specified, stochastic output without repeat-run uncertainty.

evidence.quote: However, the lack of abstraction, summarization, and reflection on erroneous cases limits the ability to fully leverage valuable insights from mistakes.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest-neighbor limitation is author characterization; Agent Hospital and related originals absent.

evidence.support_explanation: Negative component result is retained in analysis; structured residual discussion is not independently sufficient.

signatures.object: CorrectKB success summaries and ChainKB error-reflection memory
signatures.information: Medical training questions, specialist debate, lead consensus, correct answers and retrospective errors.
signatures.operation: Judge final answer against correct result; summarize successful final round or all-round failure analysis; append to separate banks; cosine-retrieve top5 from both for later cases.
signatures.output: Persistent structured text entries containing question/answer/summary or correct answer/hypothesis/analysis/final conclusion/error reflection.
signatures.conditions: Correct-result access during bank construction; trustworthy reflection and case similarity; no claim of label-free deployment.
signatures.feedback: Correct/incorrect consultation outcome and reflection over specialist reasoning.
signatures.selection_rule: Correctness routes case to success versus failure bank; no marginal utility test, conflict consolidation or rollback.
signatures.selection_data: Training-split consultations, 600 per source dataset; test accuracy curves also used to inspect bank-size saturation.
signatures.persistence: Banks survive consultation episodes; no version or retirement protocol.
signatures.later_use: Starting second round (or post-consensus reflection), retrieved cases condition specialist prompts on independent test questions.
signatures.claimed_effect: Accuracy and transferable reasoning increase with experience.
signatures.failure_boundary: Gold labels privileged; erroneous reasoning can survive correct-answer gate; reasoning transfer not isolated from example reuse.

signatures.information: Specialist views from previous two rounds organized into consistency, conflict, independence and integration.
signatures.operation: Lead physician aggregates; residual two-round context guides another round; stop at consensus or ten rounds then majority/random tie.
signatures.output: Structured debate summary and final answer reviewed for safety.
signatures.conditions: Summarizer preserves clinically relevant disagreement; consensus does not certify truth.
signatures.feedback: Other specialists’ views, not independent correctness signal inside debate.
signatures.persistence: Local debate summary; cross-task retention comes from S1, not this loop alone.
signatures.later_use: Next discussion round; final traces summarized into S1.
signatures.claimed_effect: Less context pollution and more efficient collaboration.
signatures.failure_boundary: Shared hallucination and compression loss; residual-only ablation can hurt.

gap.author_gap: Long multi-agent histories cause information pollution, while raw medical-case memory lacks abstraction and error reflection.
gap.checked_gap: Both failure modes are concrete; bank-off and module ablations support usefulness of the combined design, but no direct raw-history versus abstract-reflection memory test verifies the claimed abstraction-specific residual gap.

claims.text: The combined framework and dual experience banks improve diagnosis accuracy and rationality.
claims.setting: gpt-4-turbo; MedQA/PubMedQA test sets,600 training consultations per bank source.
claims.baseline/control: Single-model/prompts and multi-agent modules; same residual+lead with neither/one/both banks.
claims.selection_vs_test: Banks contain training experiences only per §4.1;600 chosen after performance/cost consideration; test-set sizes and overlap audits not reported.
claims.result/denominator: Both banks90.1/83.9 accuracy versus bank-off84.3/77.6; CorrectKB-only87.3/83.5, ChainKB-only85.2/78.1. Test denominators not supplied.
counterevidence: Reflection-specific improvement not isolated from additional labeled examples or prompt/call budget.
Residual-only hurts MedQA; selected correct-choice example includes incorrect disease-mechanism explanation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported retained bank benefit on later benchmark test questions, not certified correct clinical reasoning or safety.

claims.text: Knowledge banks encapsulate transferable abstract reasoning rather than isolated consultation data.
claims.setting: Banks constructed on one dataset and applied on the other with gpt-4-turbo.
claims.baseline/control: Same target framework without bank versus cross-source bank and in-domain bank.
claims.selection_vs_test: Source training experiences to different dataset test questions; contamination/pretraining overlap not audited.
claims.result/denominator: Cross-source improves MedQA84.3→87.9 and PubMedQA77.6→79.7, versus own-source90.1/83.9.
counterevidence: No raw-case retrieval, shuffled-label or reflection-removed controls to establish abstract reasoning rather than medical examples.
No interval, repeated bank-construction seed or stream-order distribution.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Cross-dataset usefulness of retained experiences reported, not mechanistic proof of abstract reasoning transfer or self-improving improver.

claims.text: Residual discussion increases efficiency while preserving useful disagreement.
claims.setting: Bounded specialist discussions with lead aggregation; subjective human assessment.
claims.baseline/control: Component ablation and observed output against single agent.
claims.selection_vs_test: Ten human questions, five clinically educated volunteers; no measured resource experiment.
claims.result/denominator: Residual-only negative on MedQA; human efficiency relatively low.
counterevidence: No latency/call/token/all-in construction costs; subjective efficiency unfavorable.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A bounded context-management design, not demonstrated resource efficiency.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Training-built non-weight knowledge banks improve later same-framework test accuracy, with bank-off controls and cross-dataset reuse; abstract reasoning, safety and efficiency claims exceed these results.
unresolved: Outcome gate main-text/appendix inconsistency; no raw-case or alternate reflection control, independent final test after construction-count choice, uncertainty, store hygiene or cost ledger.
No improved improvement mechanism evaluated: not improver. All empirical results author-reported, no reproduction.
